With notice given today, 10 October 2026, and a two-month notice period, the earliest safe end date is 10 December 2026, though the landlord could agree in writing to something earlier. I should reply to the tenant confirming this, email the landlord, and set follow-ups for the checkout inspection and key return.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. We have your notice dated 10 October 2026.

Since May this year, tenants need to give two months' written notice, not one. So the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026, and rent stays payable up to then. Your landlord can agree to an earlier date in writing. We are asking him now about 10 November and will tell you his answer. Until he agrees, please plan around 10 December.

What we are starting now:
- Checkout inspection: we will arrange this for your final day and write to you with a date and time.
- Keys: please bring all sets back to us at checkout, or we will confirm a drop-off arrangement with the checkout details. Please don't post them through the door.
- Deposit: it is held in mydeposits. After checkout, any deductions are agreed with you, or decided by the scheme's free dispute service if we can't agree. It is returned within 10 days of agreement.

You will next hear from us once we have the landlord's reply, and by 14 October at the latest.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

Hi Ben,

Tom Achterberg at Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road gave written notice by email on 10 October 2026, saying he will leave on 10 November (new job in Manchester). Under the Renters' Rights Act tenants must give two months' notice, so the earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026.

Question: do you agree in writing to the earlier date of 10 November 2026? Yes or no please, by 14 October. Without your written agreement we are working to 10 December.

Already started: acknowledged to Tom with the valid date, checkout inspection and key return being scheduled against 10 December, and Tom told his deposit (£2,019, mydeposits) is returned through the scheme after checkout. Next we will confirm the checkout date with you both.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

Book checkout inspection and key return for Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road against end date 10 Dec 2026 (or earlier date if landlord agrees in writing); give tenant 24h+ written notice; start deposit return via mydeposits after checkout

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date?
answers.answer: No. One month is too short under the Renters' Rights Act, which requires two months' written notice. Earliest end date is 10 December 2026, assuming notice was served by email on 10 Oct.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only the landlord agreeing in writing to an earlier date, such as 10 Nov. The tenant stays liable for rent until the valid end date unless the landlord agrees. We have asked him.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to Tom with the valid date, the early-date request, key return at checkout, and the deposit route (mydeposits, ADR if disputed, return within 10 days of agreement). Emailed Ben Hartley asking for a yes/no by 14 Oct. Scheduled the landlord chase and the checkout/key-return booking.

content.thinking:
With notice given today, 10 October 2026, and a two-month notice period, the earliest safe end date is 10 December 2026, though the landlord could agree in writing to something earlier. I should reply to the tenant confirming this, email the landlord, and set follow-ups for the checkout inspection and key return.

I'll note that key return arrangements will be confirmed closer to checkout since I don't have the office address handy, mention that rent continues until the end date without committing to a specific deposit figure, and note deposit return within 10 days of agreement.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. We have your notice dated 10 October 2026.

Since May this year, tenants need to give two months' written notice, not one. So the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026, and rent stays payable up to then. Your landlord can agree to an earlier date in writing. We are asking him now about 10 November and will tell you his answer. Until he agrees, please plan around 10 December.

What we are starting now:
- Checkout inspection: we will arrange this for your final day and write to you with a date and time.
- Keys: please bring all sets back to us at checkout, or we will confirm a drop-off arrangement with the checkout details. Please don't post them through the door.
- Deposit: it is held in mydeposits. After checkout, any deductions are agreed with you, or decided by the scheme's free dispute service if we can't agree. It is returned within 10 days of agreement.

You will next hear from us once we have the landlord's reply, and by 14 October at the latest.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

Hi Ben,

Tom Achterberg at Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road gave written notice by email on 10 October 2026, saying he will leave on 10 November (new job in Manchester). Under the Renters' Rights Act tenants must give two months' notice, so the earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026.

Question: do you agree in writing to the earlier date of 10 November 2026? Yes or no please, by 14 October. Without your written agreement we are working to 10 December.

Already started: acknowledged to Tom with the valid date, checkout inspection and key return being scheduled against 10 December, and Tom told his deposit (£2,019, mydeposits) is returned through the scheme after checkout. Next we will confirm the checkout date with you both.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

Book checkout inspection and key return for Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road against end date 10 Dec 2026 (or earlier date if landlord agrees in writing); give tenant 24h+ written notice; start deposit return via mydeposits after checkout
